The CPRS was the policy taken by Labor under Rudd to the 2007 election to place a mechanism for pricing carbon emissions. Faced with the option of having to make a deal with either the Coalition or the Greens to pass the bill, Rudd chose the Coalition, who under Malcolm Turnbull's leadership was prepared to work with the government. Dissatisfaction with Turnbull's decision was the straw which broke the camel's back for his leadership for many Liberals, leading to Tony Abbott's challenge, after which it took him literally 24 hours to vote down the legislation, with the support of the Greens.

Now the Greens of course were opposing the policy for different reasons to Abbott. Clearly they believed in having a carbon price or ETS or some sought, but opposed the legislation because Rudd was reluctant to give the Greens too many concessions (likely for political reasons - look at home the press treated Gillard when she negotiated with the Greens). This was a misstep from Rudd, and ultimately played a part in his removal as PM.

The Greens clearly aren't to blame for Rudd or Labor's political errors, but they should be judged by their own. The way I see it, Abbott made it perfectly clear that the Coalition would not be supporting any form of a carbon tax so long as he was leader. By voting with the Liberals to block Labor's CPRS, the Greens basically gave Abbott a win straight off the bat (imagine how humiliating it would have been for Abbott to take the leadership from Turnbull on the grounds of stopping a carbon price, only to have the Greens pass legislation a day later), AND turned down an offer from the only one of the two major parties who was actually open to placing any sought of real carbon reduction scheme.

There's a saying that politics is the art of the possible. Whether you support the Greens or not, it's clear they did not, nor are they going to any time soon, have an absolute majority in either House of Parliament. Therefore, if they are going to make real change to Australia, they have to negotiate with major parties, and it's pretty obvious to anyone who's been paying even minor attention to Australian politics for the last five or six years that Labor was far more willing to negotiate a carbon tax than Tony Abbott's Liberals were.

It's a hypothetical what would have happened if the Greens voted to pass Rudd's CPRS in 2009. Maybe Abbott would have won the next election anyway and repealed it, and we wouldn't be in a much different situation to what has panned out. But at least Rudd and Labor were trying, and considering how much Labor had to screw up to get Tony Abbott into an electable position, there's a pretty good chance that had the Greens backed Rudd's bill nearly 6 years ago, an ETS would now be firmly a part of our economy, and pretty much impossible to repeal even if a government wished to.
Why aren't the Greens scrutinised more over their decision to oppose Rudd's Emission Trading Scheme way back back in 2009?
